```{r setup, include=FALSE}
install.packages("tidyverse")

```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.

## Student performance data test. Trying out the possibilities of R!

Initially, read the data set for student performance:

```{r}
library(readr)
student_performance_data <- read_csv("data/student_performance_dataset.csv")
```

Now, create the histogram from the sleeping hours:

```{r}
hist(student_performance_data$sleep_hours)
```

Create a customized histogram from the attendance percent:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
# Create a custom histogram of the attendance percent.
student_performance_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x=attendance_percent)) +
  geom_histogram(fill="lightblue", color="blue", binwidth =20) +
  theme_classic()
```

Check the median and the quartal interval for the attendance percent:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
student_performance_data |>
  summarise(attendance_percent_median=median(attendance_percent), 
            attendance_percent_IQR=IQR(attendance_percent))
```

Create a box plot of study time hours related to attendance percent:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
student_performance_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x=study_time_hours, y=attendance_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group=study_time_hours),
               fill="skyblue1") +
  theme_classic()
```

Group student performance by study time hours:

```{r}
student_performance_data |>
  group_by(study_time_hours) |>
  summarise(attendance_percent_median=median(attendance_percent),
            attendance_percent_IQR=IQR(attendance_percent))
```

Create AES-plot on how sleeping hours affect the final exam score:

```{r}
student_performance_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x=sleep_hours, y=final_exam_score)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") +
  theme_classic()
```
